Usage: pty events [--all | <ref>] [--recent [--type <type>]] [--json] [--wait <type>] [-t <sec>]

Follow a session's event log (bell, title, notifications, tag/rename changes, user.* events).

Flags:
  --all                Follow every session, interleaved (omit <ref>)
  --recent             Print recent events and exit (don't follow)
  --json               Emit raw JSONL
  --type <type>         With --recent, print every retained event of this exact type
  --wait <type>        Replay current-generation retained matches, then wait for a match
  -t, --timeout <sec>  Timeout (seconds) for --wait or follow; exit 1 on timeout

Options may appear before or after <ref>; any other argument is an error. A named
follow exits when the session exits, its daemon vanishes without recording an
exit, or its registry entry is removed outside a locked respawn; --all continues
watching new sessions. Terminal metadata is followed by a final event-log drain.
Waits subscribe before checking durable current-generation events, recheck after
subscription and before timeout, and follow safely for any event type. session_exit
also checks recorded exit metadata if the event log is gone.
--wait exits 0 on a match, 1 on timeout/general failure (including an initially
missing session), and 2 if the target vanishes without a recorded exit, including
removal while waiting. Vanished is not successful completion.
Text and JSON streaming exit cleanly with 0 when the stdout reader closes, even idle.

Examples:
  pty events myserver
  pty events --recent --json myserver
  pty events --recent --json --type user.tests-passed myserver

Durable completion observation (inspect the recorded exit code separately):
  pty events --recent --type session_exit --json REF
  pty events --wait session_exit -t SECONDS --json REF
  pty events --recent --type session_exit --json REF
Check retained current-generation events first; if none match, use a bounded wait
and a final durable recheck. An empty --recent result is not proof of completion.
